fields.article_type: Type of article: one of 'primary data', 'review', 'meta-analysis', 'comment/editorial', or 'preprint'. Base this on the study design, not the journal section.
fields.methodology: Primary experimental method(s) used, e.g. snRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, GWAS, proteomics, patch-seq, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry. List multiple if applicable.
fields.n_donors: Number of unique donors or subjects (human or animal) in the study (integer or range). Use null if not reported.
fields.n_samples: Number of biological samples or tissue sections profiled (e.g. '140 postmortem brain samples'). Use null if not reported.
fields.n_cells: Number of cells or nuclei profiled in single-cell or spatial experiments (e.g. '468,727 nuclei'). Use null if not a single-cell/spatial study or not reported.
fields.key_cell_types: Cell types specifically implicated in schizophrenia by this study. For each, note the direction of effect where reported: gain or loss of proportion, strongest differential expression signal, upregulated or downregulated transcriptional state. E.g. 'upper-layer GABAergic neurons: reduced proportion, strongest DE signal; excitatory neurons: downregulated synaptic genes'. Use null if not applicable.
fields.key_genes: Specific genes or gene sets highlighted as relevant to schizophrenia (e.g. 'SNAP-associated genes, NRXN1'). Use null if none highlighted.
fields.genetics_integration: Any analysis linking molecular findings to schizophrenia genetics, e.g. enrichment of GWAS hits in DE genes, cell-type-specific heritability enrichment (LDSC), overlap with rare variant genes, or PRS associations. Describe the method and direction of result. Use null if no genetics integration was performed.
fields.summary: 2-3 sentence plain-language summary of the main finding and its relevance to schizophrenia, written for a genomics supervisor doing weekly triage.
